continue.description: Default true. false stops Claude entirely after the hook runs, and beats an event-specific decision. It does not by itself block a PreToolUse tool call.

stopReason.description: Shown to the user when continue is false. It stays in the conversation, so Claude sees it later.

systemMessage.description: A warning shown to the user, not added to Claude's context. Capped at 10,000 characters; longer text is saved to a file and replaced by its path and a 2,000 character preview.

terminalSequence.description: A terminal escape sequence Claude Code emits for the hook: only OSC 0, 1, 2, 9, 99, 777 and BEL. Anything else makes the field ignored. Interactive sessions only, and not from an async hook.

permissionDecision.description: allow skips the permission prompt (deny and ask rules still apply); deny prevents the call; ask prompts the user; defer ends the turn so the call can resume later, in -p mode with a single tool call only.

permissionDecisionReason.description: For deny, shown to Claude. For ask, shown to the user in the prompt. For allow and defer, written to the debug log only.

updatedInput.description: Replaces the tool's whole input before it runs, so include the unchanged fields. Pair with allow to auto-approve or ask to show the user. Ignored with defer.

additionalContext.description: Text added to Claude's context next to the tool result, wrapped in a system reminder and not shown as a chat message. State facts rather than give commands. Capped at 10,000 characters.

decision.description: Deprecated on this event: maps to allow and deny. Use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision.

title: PreToolUse hook output
description: Allows, denies, asks about or defers the tool call, and can rewrite its input. Exit code 2 denies, with stderr shown to Claude. When hooks disagree, deny beats defer, which beats ask, which beats allow. Printing nothing leaves the call to the normal permission flow.
